working_diagnosis_by_ECG.NSTE-ACS: Associated with normal ECG or ST-segment depression

hs-cTn_levels.Non-elevated: Typical for NSTE-ACS working diagnosis when troponin not elevated
hs-cTn_levels.Rise_and_fall: Typical for STEMI (rise and fall pattern of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin)

content.summary: Patients with suspected ACS are initially classified by ECG at presentation (normal, ST-depression, ST-elevation, malignant arrhythmia) to guide immediate management. After troponin results are available, patients are further classified by presence/absence and pattern (rise and fall) of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin to distinguish unstable angina, NSTEMI, and STEMI. These ECG and troponin features are used for triage and initial management and help guide subsequent common pathway treatment for ACS.
